name: Banh dap
summary: Bánh đập is the Cẩm Nam cracker you break by hand: a crisp grilled rice-paper sheet clapped to a soft steamed sheet. The dip is anchovy sauce. Two publishers print two different mixes.
origin: Cẩm Nam, Hoi An. The Hoi An World Heritage conservation centre’s 30 May 2023 article traces the cracker to that village. Danang Fantasticity’s 16 April 2024 essay also describes a Da Nang bánh tráng đập. That account stays on the Da Nang side.
texture: The 30 May 2023 article says both sheets are white rice soaked two to three hours. The crisp sheet is grilled. The inner sheet is soft. You press the middle so the crisp sheet shatters onto the soft one.
taste: The 30 May 2023 dip is mắm cái from Cửa Đại anchovy, a little sugar, and fried-shallot oil, with fresh chili or chili sauce if you want heat.

Danang Fantasticity’s Hội An section uses mắm nêm from anchovy with a little sugar, pineapple or lime, and red chili. The conservation centre’s 7 June 2023 list also spreads the soft sheet with scallion fat, shrimp powder, or pork. All three stay.
howToEat: Press the cracker with your hand, then dip, or spoon the sauce over.
Eat it with hến xào when the stall sets the clams beside it.
where: Cẩm Nam. A house number and the hour are Check on arrival.
